title: Unverified claim: proposed military tribunals for civilian immigration cases
description_short: The supplied claim alleges a February 2025 proposal to use military tribunals for civilian immigration cases.
description_medium: The supplied record alleges that the Trump administration considered using military tribunals to decide ordinary civilian immigration cases in February 2025, bypassing the immigration-court system. The input describes a proposal, not an implemented policy, but provides no source URLs, document, named official, or precise proposal date. The claim and its asserted rationale remain unverified.
description_long: An unverified claim in the frozen input says that, in February 2025, the Trump administration floated using military tribunals to adjudicate civilian immigration cases instead of the federal immigration courts. The packet gives no originating memo, named official, quoted announcement, court filing, or source URL establishing that this proposal was made. It therefore cannot support a factual account of who proposed the idea, what legal mechanism was contemplated, who would be covered, or whether any agency acted on it. The original synopsis also states that immigration-court backlogs motivated the proposal and that constitutional scholars objected; neither point has source-level support in this packet and both are omitted from the narrative. The proposal must not be described as an enacted policy, tribunal proceeding, or settled administration decision. A February 2025 report found during research discussed an outside contractor’s mass-deportation plan and proposals for mass immigration hearings, not military tribunals; it is a different proposal and does not substantiate this entry. Day-level timing, authorship, scope, legal analysis, and any subsequent action are unknown. This is an internal draft based solely on the supplied allegation, pending a matching primary document or reliable report.

title: Unverified claim: DOJ directive not to enforce multiple injunctions
description_short: The supplied entry alleges that Pam Bondi directed DOJ not to enforce several federal injunctions in March 2025.
description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that Attorney General Pam Bondi directed the Department of Justice in March 2025 not to enforce several injunctions blocking Trump administration actions. The packet contains no directive, quoted statement, case list, or source URL, and does not identify which orders were covered. Treat the broad policy claim as unverified; do not state that DOJ adopted it.
description_long: The supplied record alleges that Attorney General Pam Bondi instructed the Department of Justice in March 2025 to decline to enforce multiple federal injunctions blocking administration actions. It also attributes to DOJ a position that courts had exceeded their authority, but the frozen packet supplies no memorandum, public statement, court filing, or linked reporting for that alleged instruction. It does not name the injunctions, cases, judges, affected policies, or dates needed to test whether this was a department-wide directive or a description of separate litigation positions. The accompanying claims about a two-tier legal system, historical comparison, contempt threats, and appellate compliance orders are not independently supported in the packet and are not repeated as established facts here. Research surfaced coverage of a different dispute over March 2025 deportation flights and Judge James Boasberg’s stop order; that specific episode cannot establish the broader Bondi directive asserted by this entry, so it is not substituted as the record’s event. The date is only precise to March in the source text, and the alleged policy, scope, reasons, court responses, and outcome remain unresolved. This is an internal draft of a supplied allegation only.

title: Unverified claim: FBI surveillance of protest organizers
description_short: The supplied record alleges a February 2025 FBI directive to monitor protest organizers as potential domestic terrorists.
description_medium: The frozen record alleges that Trump instructed the FBI in February 2025 to surveil protest organizers and classify them as potential domestic terrorists, with cases opened under FBI Director Kash Patel. It further alleges monitoring of communications, finances, and associations. No directive, case records, named affected organizers, source URLs, or excerpts accompany the claim, so these details remain unverified.
description_long: According to the supplied record, Trump allegedly directed the FBI in February 2025 to monitor organizers protesting administration policies and classify them as potential domestic terrorists. The same claim says the FBI under Director Kash Patel opened cases and tracked organizers’ communications, financial transactions, and associations. The packet contains no directive, case numbers, records, named subjects, source URLs, or source excerpts to establish those assertions. It also does not identify which protests, organizations, dates, or FBI units were involved. Research surfaced a September 2025 presidential memorandum directing investigations into political violence, but that later text concerns a different date and stated subject; it cannot substantiate or replace the alleged February action. The supplied claim therefore remains an allegation rather than a verified account. Its exact date, scope, legal authority, number of affected people, and whether any cases were opened or surveillance occurred are unknown. This card is an internal draft so editors can seek a primary directive, case record, or contemporaneous report before publication.
